summary: On one day in December 1914 the Board licensed the animals of Noe Valley: a cow and a goat at 919 Alvarado Street, two horses on Jersey, one on Clipper, three on Twenty-sixth, one on Dolores. Charles Clancy kept a horse and a cow on Duncan Street, and Frank Labrucherie kept fourteen horses at 242 Chattanooga. In 1915 the city was buying its way through the blocks between Church and Dolores to build the Church Street line of the Municipal Railway, blasting as it went — and it let the Kawendee Club hold a masquerade ball on Twenty-fourth Street without the usual fee, because the takings were going to charity.
